answer.origin: NVIDIA representative, in a statement to Tom's Hardware (tomshardware.com), stated 2026-07-06 and published 2026-07-06, responding to reports that the Kyber rack for Rubin Ultra was delayed to 2028.
answer.note: On 2026-07-06 an NVIDIA representative told Tom's Hardware only that 'Our roadmap is intact,' with no further detail. The statement is a party denial of roadmap problems, and it sits against a same-day SemiAnalysis-based report (relayed by The Decoder) that Kyber NVL144 slipped more than twelve months to 2028 and that the four-die Rubin Ultra was canceled. The denial does not establish that Kyber is on schedule or that the SemiAnalysis report is wrong, because it names no product, date or mitigation. The usable conclusion is narrow: NVIDIA publicly asserted on 2026-07-06 that its roadmap is intact, which weakens but does not resolve the reported Kyber delay. For the Data Center revenue question (v6), this item adds no quantity, so it does not move the FY2027 estimate.
limitations: The statement does not say which roadmap items it covers, so it cannot be confirmed as a statement about Kyber, Rubin Ultra or the NVL72x2 design.
No timing, product schedule or mitigation is given, so the statement cannot confirm or refute the reported 2028 Kyber date.
The statement is a single unsupported assertion with no disclosed basis or named speaker beyond 'NVIDIA representative'.
The statement carries no Data Center revenue, supply or demand figure, so it does not inform the FY2027 revenue question quantitatively.
follow_up: Check NVIDIA's official product roadmap, investor materials and any earnings-call remarks after 2026-07-06 for a specific Kyber NVL144 or Rubin Ultra schedule.
Check whether the NVIDIA representative's statement was later clarified or expanded in other outlets or filings.
Compare any subsequent SemiAnalysis, supplier or cloud-operator reports on Kyber PCB midplane production and NVL72x2 status against NVIDIA's official schedule.
